extracted.intended_audience: General Wikipedia readers; researchers, policymakers, potential borrowers, donors and practitioners interested in the African Development Bank
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive summary of the African Development Bank Group: history, structure, membership, mission, lending instruments, sectoral priorities, governance and key financial terms used to guide operations and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADF eligibility (countries eligible for African Development Fund resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of low-income regional member countries eligible for African Development Fund (ADF) resources (e.g., Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADF provides development finance on concessional terms to low-income RMCs that are unable to borrow on the AfDB's non-concessional terms; poverty reduction is the main aim of ADF activities. Eligibility is by country list and can include non-regional members as contributors; note explicit lists for ADF-only, blend, and ADB-only eligibility in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADF lending terms (financial terms for ADF loans)
rubrics_metrics.description: ADF lends at no interest, with an annual service charge of 0.75% and a commitment fee of 0.5%, and a 50-year repayment period including a 10-year grace period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ADF is usually replenished every three years by contributor countries; donors' replenishment levels and schedules determine the Fund's resources. Historical replenishment and donor-share information (e.g., largest ADF shareholder: United Kingdom ~14%) is relevant when planning requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nigeria Trust Fund (NTF) lending terms
rubrics_metrics.description: NTF lending: 4% interest rate with a 25-year repayment period including a five-year grace period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NTF resources are used to finance projects of national or regional importance in poorest AfDB members on concessional terms; loans can be used for concessional operations with long- and short-term maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally only African countries could join; since 1982 non-African (non-regional) countries may join. The AfDB Group comprises the African Development Bank, African Development Fund and Nigeria Trust Fund; overall membership includes regional and non-regional members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership status affects access to different windows (ADB, ADF, NTF) and governance representation. The article lists regional and non-regional member countries and eligibility notes (e.g., all AU countries except SADR eligible for NTF benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and voting power structure
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB is controlled by a Board of Executive Directors; voting power on the Board is split approximately 60% regional (African) and 40% non-regional members, with voting strength proportional to member share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member governments are represented at the Board of Governors (typically finance ministers) who meet annually; the Board of Executive Directors makes day-to-day decisions about loans and policies. Voting power distribution (and largest shareholders) influences institutional priorities and approval likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making organs and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Member governments are officially represented by their Minister of Finance/Planning/Cooperation on the Board of Governors; they typically appoint representatives to the Board of Executive Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major decisions about leadership, strategy and governing bodies are taken at the Governors' annual meetings; operational approvals are by the Executive Board. Understanding who represents a country and how voting blocs form is important for navigating approvals and policy influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of Account (XUA) and accounting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB uses a Unit of Account registered as ISO 4217 code XUA for accounting between state members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: XUA is not exchanged directly by individuals and is used for internal accounting and reporting. Proposals and financial planning should be cognizant of the Bank's accounting unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission and overarching strategic objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The AfDB's mission is to fight poverty and improve living conditions through promoting public and private capital investment in projects and programs contributing to economic and social development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align projects to poverty reduction, economic and social development objectives, and the Bank's stated priorities (including climate-related initiatives). The Bank has faced criticism (e.g., funding greenhouse-gas-intensive projects) which may affect policy scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary operational functions (types of support provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB's primary functions: making loans and equity investments, providing technical assistance, promoting investment of public and private capital, and assisting in organizing development policies. The Bank must give special attention to national and multinational projects needed to promote regional integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding requests and project designs should reflect these functions — include investment, technical assistance components, and regional integration rationale where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectoral priorities: infrastructure (power, water, sanitation, transport, communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infrastructure (including power supply, water and sanitation, transport and communications) has historically received the largest share of AfDB lending and is reaffirmed as a priority in strategic plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AfDB tends to prioritise infrastructure and regional integration projects; applicants in infrastructure sectors may find higher funding probability. The Bank is the lead agency for NEPAD infrastructure initiatives and hosts the Infrastructure Consortium for Africa (ICA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional integration as a funding priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional integration infrastructure projects are a key part of AfDB's business; transport and power interconnections help create larger markets and competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that demonstrate regional economic benefits, interconnections, or integration into RECs are aligned with AfDB priorities and may be favored for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: High 5 strategic priority areas and funding emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB's 'High 5' strategic priority areas (referenced in the article) received increased funding in 2022: renewable energy, food security, industrialization, infrastructure, etc.; renewable energy accounted for 100% of approvals for energy generation projects in that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proposals that map to the High 5 (and explicitly to renewable energy, food security, industrialization, infrastructure) will align with recent funding emphasis and may be more competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project preparation and leveraging (IPPF/ICA support)
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB helps prepare projects to obtain financing from other sources through initiatives like the Infrastructure Project Preparation Facility (IPPF) and by hosting the Infrastructure Consortium for Africa (ICA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-stage project preparation support and leveraging the Bank's instruments can improve bankability and access to co-financing; applicants should consider using Bank facilities to ready projects for financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity and country-focus in operations
rubrics_metrics.description: An emerging view (cited by the Board and management) is that AfDB should be more 'selective' and 'country-focused' in its operations, which is driving certain lending priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries and project proposals demonstrating strong alignment with a focused, country-specific development strategy and high-impact priorities may be prioritized under this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health/HIV-AIDS program policy pillars (criteria for health-related interventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AfDB's five policies for HIV/AIDS: (1) institutional capacity building for policy/strategy formulation and implementation; (2) human capital development through training and technical assistance; (3) multi-sectoral responses emphasizing prevention, STI control, VCT, infrastructure and supply of antiretroviral drugs; (4) advocacy to raise political commitment and leadership; (5) partnership development to forge and revitalize alliances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health project proposals should address one or more of these pillars explicitly, include capacity-building and multi-sectoral approaches, and demonstrate partnership and advocacy components when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of social bonds and financing instruments (COVID-era practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the coronavirus pandemic, AfDB has increasingly focused on issuing social bonds to raise funds for poor countries; example: launched a $463.9 million social bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrowers and partners should consider Bank-issued instruments (social bonds) and their thematic targeting when designing projects that address social impacts tied to crises like COVID-19.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADF replenishment and donor contribution norms
rubrics_metrics.description: ADF resources primarily come from contributions by non-African member states; the Fund is typically replenished every three years (unless members decide otherwise). Historical donor shares are noted (UK ~14%, US ~6.5%, Japan ~5.4%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding replenishment cycles and donor priorities is important for timing proposals and anticipating available concessional resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit rating and portfolio performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: AfDB has maintained a AAA credit rating; active portfolio metrics reported (e.g., active portfolio UA 44.33 billion; 58% of projects rated satisfactorily; disbursements UA 3.5 billion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bank's credit rating affects its capacity to raise funds and terms; applicants should be aware of portfolio performance indicators and the Bank's emphasis on satisfactory ratings when designing projects and reporting results.
